</medium>

3. +-when I tap it, pop up two choices: post a photo or create an event.

We're building out a proper admin backend for our image editing platform and honestly the current setup is a mess — filter management is in one place, task monitoring is somewhere else, and our team keeps wasting time jumping between screens just to do basic ops work. I need a single, well-organized admin dashboard that our operations team can live in all day without going crazy.

Here's roughly what we need covered:

**Filter Template Library** — this is the big one right now because we're about to launch paid filter packs. We need a place where we can see all filters in one grid/list view, with thumbnail previews, category tags (like portrait, landscape, vintage, commercial, etc.), subscription tier binding (free / pro / enterprise), status (live / draft / under review / delisted), and who created or uploaded it. The ops team needs to be able to directly toggle filters on/off, reassign them to different subscription tiers, and there should be a section specifically for user-submitted custom filters pending compliance review — we want to approve or reject those without leaving the page. Would be great if we can also batch-edit tier assignments when we're doing a promotion or package restructuring.

**Processing Task Queue Monitor** — we handle a ton of batch image jobs for our users and right now it's really hard to get a quick read on what's healthy vs. stuck. Ideally a live-ish queue view showing tasks with status (queued, processing, completed, failed, retrying), user ID or account name, task type (batch resize, filter apply, format convert, etc.), submitted time, elapsed time, and error codes for failed ones. We should be able to manually retry failed tasks or flag them for engineering follow-up directly from this view. Some kind of summary bar at the top showing total pending / failed count today would help a lot.

We want ops to manage this directly — add new presets (name, dimensions, aspect ratio, platform tag like "Instagram Story" or "Amazon Product"), reorder them, enable/disable them per subscription tier. Not complicated but we just need it in one place.

We don't need anything fancy here, just a user management section where we can assign roles and see who has access to what.

Overall visual vibe should be clean, professional, high information density — think dark sidebar nav, white/light gray content area, clear data tables, status badges with color coding. Not overly designed, just functional and easy to scan quickly. The sidebar should have clear module groupings. Data tables should support basic sorting and filtering. Please pre-fill some realistic-looking mock data so the whole thing feels usable and we can actually walk through the flows — fake filter names, sample task queue entries, that kind of thing.

I need something clean and structured.

Here's what I'm imagining:

**Supplier side (the submission form):**
It should walk them through steps — like a multi-step form, not just one giant page they scroll through. Step 1 is basic info: company name, contact person, supplier ID (we assign these), submission date auto-filled. Step 2 is the actual file uploads, but broken into categories — for example "Business License", "Quality Certification", "Inspection Report", "Signed Contract Annex" — each category is its own upload slot. For each slot, I want to set the allowed file types (some are PDF only, some can be PDF or Excel, one can be images) and a max file size, and if they try to upload something wrong it should immediately show an error message like "this slot only accepts PDF files, please re-upload" — not after they hit submit, right away. I also want them to see an upload progress bar so they know it's actually uploading and not just frozen. Step 3 is a review/confirmation screen where they can see everything they uploaded before they hit submit. After submitting, show them a confirmation page with a reference number.

Also important: suppliers should NOT be able to submit if any required document slot is empty. Required vs optional slots should be clearly marked. The form should feel simple enough that someone not very tech-savvy can get through it without calling me for help — clear labels, obvious error states, nothing ambiguous.

**My side (management view):**
I need a dashboard or table that shows all suppliers and their submission status at a glance. Something like: supplier name, supplier ID, submission date (or "not submitted yet"), and then a column for each document category showing green checkmark or red warning depending on whether that file was received. I want to be able to filter by status — show me only the ones with missing documents, or show me everyone who's submitted. 

For downloading: I need to be able to click on a single supplier row and download all their files as one zip package. But I also need a "select multiple" mode where I check several suppliers and batch download all their files together — this is critical because when the audit team asks me for everything, I can't be downloading 15 zips one at a time. Each downloaded file should have a standardized name automatically — like SupplierID_DocumentType_SubmissionDate — not whatever name the supplier uploaded with.

Design-wise, keep it professional and clean, nothing flashy. Maybe a neutral color scheme, clear table borders, status badges that are easy to read at a glance (like a colored pill showing "Complete", "Incomplete", "Not Submitted"). The management view should feel like an internal ops tool, not a consumer app.

One thing I keep forgetting to ask for and then regret — can the supplier submission form also handle the case where a supplier needs to resubmit one document (like they uploaded the wrong version)? Maybe allow them to replace a specific file after submission within a certain window, or at least flag it so I can manually request a reupload from the management side. Not sure exactly how that would work but some way to handle version replacement without starting over from scratch.

I'm building out the admin backend for a diet tracking app — specifically the section where operators can manage users' food logs and the food database (calories, GI index, macros, etc.). Need this to feel clean and functional, not just a basic CRUD table.

Here's what I'm thinking for the main food log management table:

**Food Log Overview Table**
- Columns: User ID / Username, Meal Type (breakfast/lunch/dinner/snack — filterable via pill tabs at top), Food Name, Calories (kcal), GI Value (with color-coded badges: low = green, medium = yellow, high = red), Portion Size, Log Timestamp, Status (Verified / Pending Review / Flagged)
- Bulk actions: bulk-approve pending entries, bulk-delete, export to CSV
- Inline row actions: quick edit, delete, flag for review
- Clicking a row should expand an inline panel (not navigate away) showing full nutritional breakdown — carbs, protein, fat, fiber — and any user notes

**Filtering & Search**
- Left sidebar filter panel: date range picker, meal type checkboxes, calorie range slider (0–2000+ kcal), GI level (low/medium/high), entry status
- Top search bar: search by food name or username, with debounced autocomplete
- Active filters shown as dismissible tags below the search bar
- "Reset All Filters" button that clears everything but keeps pagination state

**Food Database Management Panel** (separate tab or section)
- Searchable table of all food items in the system: Name, Category, Calories/100g, GI Score, Verified (yes/no toggle)
- Admins can add new food items via a side drawer form — required fields are Name, Category, Calories, Carbs, Protein, Fat; optional fields GI Score and Notes
- Validation: calories field must be numeric and > 0, GI score 0–100, form should show inline errors on blur not just on submit
- If a food item is being used in any active user logs, deleting it should show a warning modal with a count of affected records, not just silently delete

**States & Edge Cases**
- Empty state for the log table when filters return no results — show a helpful "No logs match your filters" message with a reset button, not just a blank table
- Loading skeleton for the table rows during data fetch
- If a user has flagged entries, show a badge on their username in the table
- Pagination at bottom, show "Showing X–Y of Z results", page size selector (25 / 50 / 100)
- Toast notifications for all actions (approve, delete, save edits) — success and error variants

Design-wise: keep it neutral and professional, dark sidebar with white content area, good use of whitespace, tables shouldn't feel cramped. No flashy animations, just subtle transitions on drawer open/close and row expand.
